headline: $400,000 for school resource officer salaries and curriculum approved
summary: The $293,000 covers school resource officer salaries for the 26-27 year, and $107,000 goes to curriculum purchases. The $400,000 came from the city's health insurance fund to cover a net school spending shortfall. Members also referred a discussion of e-bikes and e-scooters to the Public Facilities and Safety Subcommittee. The superintendent's proposed goals for 2026-2027 come back for a vote in December.
decisions: Approved $400,000 split: $293,000 for school resource officer salaries and $107,000 for curriculum, unanimously.
Referred discussion of e-bikes and e-scooters to the Public Facilities and Safety Subcommittee, unanimously.
discussion: Superintendent's proposed goals: Members asked how progress on the induction program goal could be measured and how students would take part in the special education goal. The goals come back for a vote in December, and suggested changes can be sent before then.

School resource officer report: The superintendent reported $312,871.81 in officer costs last year, seven court referrals, and one school-based arrest. Some offenses may have been coded wrong in the student information system, and the district is checking its records with police.

E-bikes and e-scooters: Members said a one-day state police operation with Everett, Medford, and Malden happened last week and may happen again in the spring. Members said a city ordinance bars motorized scooters from school grounds, parks, and playgrounds, and a meeting on the issue will be scheduled with the police chief invited.

Public comment on city lawsuit: A public speaker said the school district sued a resident in 2021 over public records requests, and that a recent appellate decision says a records holder cannot sue a requester. The speaker said the district has spent more than $200,000 on the case and the family intends to get that money back.

School calendar for 2027-28: A survey on the calendar is open through Friday, November 20, after a forum drew about 65 people two weeks ago. A suggestion was raised to consider giving up a February or April vacation to cover religious holidays, and the superintendent said the survey is already out.
